The closest matches compare fine-tuning or domain adaptation for legal text representations, but they do not all focus on vector embeddings across diverse domains in the same way. One paper shows that legal-domain fine-tuning of multilingual embedding models improves retrieval, with especially strong gains in low-resource languages and transfer to unseen languages [1]. Another compares a base retriever, a legal-only fine-tuned model, and a mixed fine-tuned model for Brazilian legal search, finding legal-only training best for specialized tasks while mixed training is more robust across heterogeneous search types and out-of-domain evaluation [2].

Other papers address related trade-offs rather than broad embedding utility: full fine-tuning outperforms LoRA for unfair ToS detection, though LoRA uses less memory [3]; continued pretraining improves masked-token loss for Russian legal documents but the paper says it does not establish practical legal utility [4]; and a domain-adapted embedding model yields gains on a supervision-aligned Brazilian legal subset while BM25 stays competitive elsewhere [6].
